summary.text: The paranoid King of Argos who locked his daughter Danae in a bronze chamber to prevent a prophecy that his grandson would kill him. He was killed by Perseus' stray discus.

story.text: Acrisius fought a bitter war against his twin brother Proetus for the throne of Argos. When an oracle warned him that a son born to his daughter Danae would kill him, he locked her away in a subterranean bronze chamber.

Despite his precautions, Danae gave birth to Perseus. Acrisius threw both mother and child into the sea in a wooden chest. Years later, his fears came true: while attending athletic games in Larissa, Perseus accidentally struck Acrisius with a discus, fulfilling the prophecy.
